title: MR enterography (small bowel MRI)
what: An MRI of the belly, for which you first drink a special solution. It opens up the bowel so it can be seen well in the images.
why: Most often for inflammatory bowel disease, to look at the small bowel without radiation.
duration: drinking the solution takes about an hour, the MRI itself 30 to 45 minutes, the report in a few days
tell_doctor: If you have a pacemaker or metal in your body
If you are afraid of closed spaces
If you have kidney disease or an allergy to contrast
If you have glaucoma or an enlarged prostate - because of the medicine for the bowel

prepare.title: Fasting
prepare.text: Usually no food for 4 to 6 hours. Ask the clinic.

prepare.title: Time
prepare.text: Arrive early: you drink the solution for about an hour before the exam.

prepare.title: Metal
prepare.text: Take off jewelry, watch and belt.

bring: A change of underwear - the solution is a laxative
steps: You drink the solution in small portions over about an hour
You change clothes and remove metal
You lie on the table - often on your stomach
A catheter is placed in your vein
A medicine to stop the bowel moving and contrast are given
Pictures are taken, often while you hold your breath
feel: Drinking so much is unpleasant, and you may feel bloated
The medicine can blur your vision for a while
Warmth when the contrast goes in
after: After the exam you may have loose stools - stay near a toilet
Do not drive while your vision is blurry
The report is usually ready in a few days
red_flags: Eye pain and a sudden drop in vision after the exam - call your local emergency number
Rash, swelling of the face or trouble breathing - call your local emergency number

faq.a: Without it the bowel is collapsed and is hard to see in the images.

faq.q: Can I go to work right after?
faq.a: Usually yes, but keep in mind you may have loose stools.

reminders.text: MR enterography tomorrow. Do not eat for 4 to 6 hours before, and arrive early - you will need to drink the solution.
